analysis:
This PR contains only documentation and changelog edits: two new changelog.d fragments and a docs/developer/build.md update (date stamp plus a paragraph after line 243 about rebuilding the provider test product before running the authorization guidance tests). No executable code is visible, so I found no concrete security regression, new attack surface or invalidated threat assumption.

The two changelog fragments describe provider CLI behavior that is not visible in the supplied diff. `darkbloom status` and `darkbloom doctor` would keep reporting App Attest authorization until the coordinator lease expires, instead of requiring a renewal within 10 seconds. They would also stop offering MDM removal when the coordinator decision is too old. The text states that `darkbloom unenroll` keeps its 10-second renewal requirement and its existing checks.

Relevant threat IDs are T-053, T-057, T-052 and TB-011. The changelog text is consistent with them: status display is diagnostic only, and the fragments do not describe authorization changes.

The corresponding Swift source (status, doctor and unenroll decision code) was not supplied. The fragments' claims that the change is display-only, that unenroll is unchanged and that serving authorization is unaffected are therefore unverified. A later source-pass or integration reviewer should check those claims if the Swift changes are in the batch. In particular, check that the lease-expiry display logic does not feed any authorization or removal gate, and that the unenroll path still enforces its 10-second readiness check.

The build.md edit references test.md#provider-authorization-guidance, which is not in this diff; this is a documentation link only.
